k:multilingual-eval-faq@1.1:c080929d.excerpt:
## Register and honorifics

### Q: Who scores Korean or Japanese register shifts?
Route the case to appropriate Korean or Japanese language QA with exact sentence endings and surrounding context. Check quotations and addressee changes. The task-quality grade depends on demonstrated impact; do not assign a major penalty from the presence of a shift alone.

### Q: Spanish tú versus usted inconsistency — major or minor?
Ask Spanish QA to check addressee, intended formality and discourse context. An unjustified shift can be an error, but its grade needs a case-specific rationale.

# Japanese register review awaiting complete context

## Case packet
M11-JA-022 was reported as starting in です/ます and ending in plain form. The supplied excerpt omitted the preceding dialogue and did not establish whether the closing sentence addressed the same person.

## TL routing
Alex assigned the review to Yuki (U019, Japanese QA). Yuki requested the complete dialogue before deciding whether the change was purposeful. The follow-up was due September 30; this record contains no completed assessment.

## State
The case was routed, not resolved. No major/minor score or general keigo rule was approved. A due date is a requested follow-up time, not proof that the follow-up occurred.

[PRIOR RECORD (expert_review; decision_status: tl_approved; execution_status: assessment_recorded; outcome_status: resolved_for_scoped_case) - history, not a standing rule.]
# Scoped Korean finding confirmed by the TL

## Specialist finding
Hana reviewed the complete paragraph for M10-KO-017. The casual sentence was a quoted utterance from a different speaker, and the surrounding narration retained its polite register. She found no unsupported shift by the narrator.

## TL confirmation
Alex confirmed no register-consistency penalty for this exact quoted-speaker case. The finding does not authorize a casual switch while addressing the same person without a discourse reason.

## Result and limits
The batch-10 question for M10-KO-017 is resolved. Later same-addressee cases require their own context; an older favorable ruling cannot be transferred merely because both texts contain polite and casual endings.

k:multilingual-eval-instructions@1.2:e19.excerpt:
## Register and honorifics
Check the addressee, discourse context, quotation and intended register. A speaker change or quotation can justify a shift. Provide exact sentence endings and route locale-specific scoring to the appropriate language QA. An apparent shift is not an automatic major penalty.

# Korean register case referred to language QA

## Request
M10-KO-017 contains a polite narrative followed by a casual sentence inside quotation marks. The packet did not identify whether the quoted speaker and addressee changed.

## TL decision
Alex routed the case to Hana (U008), whose recorded specialty is Korean, with the exact endings and surrounding paragraph. Do not assign a major register penalty from the ending change alone.

## Requested assessment
Establish who is speaking, whether the quote is intentional, and whether the language remains appropriate for the intended audience. The original scoring question stays open until that context is reviewed.

## Scope
This referral concerns M10-KO-017 in batch 10. It is not a general exemption for Korean register shifts.
